extensionTypes.Agent: LLM-driven, multi-step, open-ended reasoning (a mapped skill runs in the provisioning ticket).
extensionTypes.Worker: Deterministic background job: pure compute or reconcile/apply-with-retry, no LLM.
extensionTypes.Passthrough: One external object created/updated/deleted synchronously, no agent, no loop.
extensionTypes.No-provision: Observe-only or provision-on-demand-later; nothing fires on save.

classifications.generic: Mechanism has no hardcoded business logic for one customer; swap config/credentials and it works anywhere with the same scope.
classifications.customer-specific: Hardcoded to one customer's app names, tenant layout, or business process.

extensions.name: RDS Major-Version Upgrade Orchestrator (Blue/Green)
extensions.description: Orchestrates a near-zero-downtime RDS major-version upgrade via AWS Blue/Green Deployments instead of in-place (avoiding 10-30+ min hard downtime on a single-AZ payment-rail DB): precheck -> manual snapshot -> target parameter group -> create B/G deployment (guarded by a tenant-scoped IAM Deny on duplomaster so Duplo's own reconciler doesn't delete the green instance mid-creation) -> validate -> switchover -> post-verify -> cleanup (guard removed). v1 shipped as a single-shot automated run, no human-approval gate (see notes).
extensions.notes: BUILT 2026-09-16 as extensions/rdsupgrade/ in this devkit repo (duplo.examples.rdsupgrade v0.1.1), hot-loaded onto helpdesk-dev01.test21-apps.duplocloud.net / prasanna-ws. Internal/proof-of-concept only, not customer-facing. Scope change during build: the originally-planned two-gate approval design (ApproveCutover/ApproveCleanup) was dropped for v1 -- ResourceWorkerBase's multi-tick 'wait indefinitely across ticks' semantics could not be verified (the AI Studio backend source isn't checked out anywhere locally, and neither dev-kit worker sample exercises anything longer than an instant one-shot compute), so v1 runs the whole pipeline automatically in one ApplyAsync call with in-call AWS polling instead of cross-tick waiting. Re-add the approval gate before ever pointing this at a real customer database. AWS Blue/Green supports MySql/PostgreSql/MariaDB/AuroraMySql/AuroraPostgreSql only (confirmed against the DuploCloud backend's own RDSConfiguration.SupportsBlueGreenDeployment()); v1 is tested MySQL-only, schema is engine-parametric. The delete-guard (formerly tracked as a separate #37) is folded in as an internal step -- confirmed via the duplo repo's native AwsRdsBlueGreenManager/RdsBlueGreenApiController that its orphan-protection only covers deployments created through ITS OWN manager (LocalHost-auth-only, feature-flagged off, unreachable from an extension), so our own IAM-Deny guard stays necessary permanently, not just as a stopgap. Verified live: clean build (backend + Angular Native Federation frontend), deployed, registered, and a real create->fail->cleanup test run surfaced a genuine bug (initial AWS-client-resolution sat outside the try/catch, so a scope failure left Result.Phase stuck at 'Requested' with empty StepHistory despite the resource showing Failed) -- fixed, redeployed as v0.1.1, re-verified clean. NOT yet tested: the real AWS happy path -- prasanna-ws has no AWS scope attached, so live RDS calls are unverified. Research precedent for the v2 approval-gate redesign: the duplo repo's native (non-extension) EksUpgradeBase -- a step-chain + persisted-progress-state + periodic-sweep reconciler. Also cross-checked 2026-09-16 against the company-wide 'Extension Use Case' Google Sheet (no duplicate ask, but a cluster of same-shaped asks: EKS Upgrade x3, AMI upgrade, Duplo-Host Patching) and ClickUp extension-testing board (NOT checked, connector not authorized this session).

extensions.name: Cloudflare Workers Watch & Governed Deploy
extensions.description: v1 Worker polls a Cloudflare account's Workers inventory, deployments and GraphQL error rates, persists deployment history and alerts to Slack on new deploys/new scripts/error spikes; v2 Agent runs a governed wrangler deploy with LLM diff review and human approval; v3 optional DNS/WAF posture audit.
extensions.notes: Sourced from Jason Brethorst (MTR) Slack ask 2026-10-13: agentic code runs on Cloudflare Workers, human apps on AWS. MTR also fronts migrated AWS apps with proxied Cloudflare DNS, so zone/DNS + SSL-mode checks move into v1. 2026-10-14: not new ground -- other-scope integrations (duploai-issue-reporter Jira/ClickUp, prd-mgmt-extension Slack, opensearch-extension, duploai-extension-pocs Jenkins, baic-uniphore OCI) and DriftCadence polling Workers (duploai-extension-pull-request-review, duploai-extension-automation) already exist in other repos. Keep the Cloudflare MCP server (AI HelpDesk) on a separate scope from the extension. Full design in EXTENSION_BACKLOG.md.
